# Python SciPy / Python SciFort timing comparison

Started: 2026-11-23T20:47:27.021283+00:00

Both backends are called from Python through their public distribution methods.
Times include Python validation, dispatch, allocation and FFI overhead.
Inputs and library loading/building are outside timings. Both backends allocate output;
SciFort does not use its optional reusable output buffer. No direct scipy.special kernels.
Each batch alternates two preconstructed inputs and consumes endpoint checksums.
Backend order alternates by sample. Ratios above one favor SciFort.

Quick smoke workloads: False. Validation-only: False.

## Summary of SciPy/SciFort time ratios

Each selected workload contributes one ratio of median elapsed times.
Statistics use unrounded ratios; values above one favor SciFort.
Mean is the arithmetic mean. SD is the sample standard deviation across
workload ratios (divisor count - 1), not uncertainty in repeated timings.
SD is n/a when a group contains only one workload.

These describe the selected workloads, rather than overall library speedups.
Each case has equal weight; category counts, API and allocation differences,
and scalar Python call overhead affect the summaries. Background CPU load
can also affect results; use an idle machine for performance comparisons.
